title: Cluster add-ons
description: The small cluster services everything depends on: CoreDNS (cluster DNS), metrics-server (resource metrics API for kubectl top/HPA), kubelet-csr-approver (approves kubelet serving certificates), local-path-provisioner (PersistentVolumes on the node disk, no metrics of its own) and the telemetry agents behind the Kubernetes dashboards (kube-state-metrics, node-exporter, scrape targets). The official kps CoreDNS dashboard stays as the detailed view.

options.content:
**What this is.** Four small services that are invisible until they break:

| Service | What breaks when it is down |
|---|---|
| **CoreDNS** (`kube-system`, 1 replica) | Every in-cluster name lookup (`svc.cluster.local`) and every lookup of external names from pods: apps fail to connect, Argo CD cannot reach GitHub. |
| **metrics-server** | `kubectl top`, HPAs, KEDA CPU/memory scalers; API discovery errors for `metrics.k8s.io` (Argo CD shows them). |
| **kubelet-csr-approver** | Nothing immediately; but when the kubelet serving certificate (~1 year) rotates, its CSR stays Pending: `kubectl logs/exec` and metrics-server stop working once the old cert expires. |
| **local-path-provisioner** | New PVCs stay Pending (existing volumes keep working). It exports **no metrics**: this dashboard watches it through kube-state-metrics, its logs and the PVC events. |

**Healthy looks like:** everything UP; DNS SERVFAIL ~0 %, p99 latency in milliseconds, cache hit ratio high; metrics-server APIService
available and scraping the kubelet every 15 s; kubelet serving certificate months from expiry; no Pending PVCs.

**When something is red:** DNS - check the upstream resolvers (forward plugin: the LAN router and a public resolver) and CoreDNS logs;
metrics-server - its logs usually show a kubelet TLS error (kubelet serving cert, see csr-approver row); local-path - the PVC
events/logs panels below say why provisioning failed (disk full, node affinity). Detailed DNS view: the kps **CoreDNS** dashboard.
Annotations: alerts of these services (red), restarts (orange), CoreDNS config reload failures (purple).

panels.title: CoreDNS
panels.description: CoreDNS metrics endpoint scraped (coredns-mixin alert CoreDNSDown when absent, https://github.com/povilasv/coredns-mixin).

panels.title: Queries / s
panels.description: DNS requests per second (`coredns_dns_requests_total`, https://coredns.io/plugins/metrics/).

panels.title: SERVFAIL ratio
panels.description:
Share of responses with rcode SERVFAIL over 5 min, formula of coredns-mixin alert
CoreDNSErrorsHigh (warning 1 %, critical 3 %, https://github.com/povilasv/coredns-mixin/blob/master/alerts/coredns.libsonnet). SERVFAIL = CoreDNS could not
answer (upstream down, loop, plugin error). NXDOMAIN is *not* an error (search-path lookups produce many). The SERVFAIL
series only exists after the first one, so 0 is shown when absent.

panels.title: Latency p99
panels.description:
99th percentile time to answer a query (`coredns_dns_request_duration_seconds`), formula of
coredns-mixin alert CoreDNSLatencyHigh (critical above 4 s, https://github.com/povilasv/coredns-mixin). Cached answers take microseconds; forwarded ones the
upstream round-trip.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description:
Share of queries answered from the cache plugin: hits / requests
(`coredns_cache_hits_total`, `coredns_cache_requests_total`, https://coredns.io/plugins/cache/). Low values mean most queries go upstream
(slower). No upstream threshold, no colour.

panels.title: Forward healthcheck broken (1h)
panels.description:
Times all upstream resolvers were marked unhealthy at once in the last hour
(`coredns_forward_healthcheck_broken_total`, https://coredns.io/plugins/forward/); counter of coredns-mixin alert
CoreDNSForwardHealthcheckBrokenCount. > 0 = external names stopped resolving for a while.

panels.title: Panics (24h)
panels.description: Recovered panics in CoreDNS plugins in 24 h (`coredns_panics_total`, https://coredns.io/plugins/metrics/). Should be 0.

panels.title: Config reload failures
panels.description:
Failed Corefile reloads since start (`coredns_reload_failed_total`, reload plugin): a
bad edit of the coredns ConfigMap is rejected and the old config keeps running.

panels.title: Responses by rcode
panels.description:
Responses per second by DNS response code (`coredns_dns_responses_total`), as in "Responses (by
rcode)" of the kps CoreDNS dashboard (https://github.com/prometheus-community/helm-charts/tree/kube-prometheus-stack-93.3.0/charts/kube-prometheus-stack/templates/grafana/dashboards-1.14/k8s-coredns.yaml). NOERROR and NXDOMAIN are normal; SERVFAIL/REFUSED are not.

panels.title: Query latency
panels.description:
p50 and p99 query latency (`coredns_dns_request_duration_seconds`). The red line marks 1 s; the
coredns-mixin CoreDNSLatencyHigh alert fires at a p99 of 4 s for 10 min.

panels.title: Upstream (forward) latency p99 and SERVFAIL
panels.description:
p99 latency per upstream resolver and the upstream SERVFAIL share,
from `coredns_proxy_request_duration_seconds{proxy_name="forward"}` (https://coredns.io/plugins/forward/; CoreDNS >= 1.11 renamed the
coredns_forward_request_* metrics used by the coredns-mixin alerts CoreDNSForwardLatencyHigh (4 s) and CoreDNSForwardErrorsHigh
(1 % / 3 %), same formulas). A slow or failing upstream makes every external lookup slow.

panels.title: metrics-server
panels.description: metrics-server /metrics scraped (ServiceMonitor from helm-charts/metrics-server).

panels.title: metrics.k8s.io API
panels.description:
Whether the API server can reach the aggregated APIService v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io served by
metrics-server (1 - `aggregator_unavailable_apiservice`). This is what `kubectl top` and HPAs use; when unavailable, API
discovery errors also show up in Argo CD. Alert KubeAggregatedAPIDown (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/system_alerts.libsonnet).

panels.title: Kubelet scrape success
panels.description:
Share of metrics-server scrapes of the kubelet (/metrics/resource) that succeeded over 5 min
(`metrics_server_kubelet_request_total` by `success`, https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server). Failures are almost always TLS (kubelet serving cert) or
the kubelet being down.

panels.title: Last kubelet scrape age
panels.description:
How old metrics-server's last kubelet scrape was at the moment Prometheus scraped
metrics-server: `timestamp(m) - m` of `metrics_server_kubelet_last_request_time_seconds` (measured at scrape time, so the
1-minute Prometheus scrape interval does not inflate it). metrics-server scrapes every `--metric-resolution` = 15 s here, so
a few seconds is normal; red after 4 missed cycles (60 s, derived from that setting).

panels.title: Pods in metrics store
panels.description:
Containers and nodes metrics-server currently holds metrics for (`metrics_server_storage_points`
by type). Containers should match roughly the running containers; 0 = `kubectl top` returns nothing.

panels.title: Scrape duration, metric freshness and tick
panels.description:
p99 duration of a kubelet scrape
(`metrics_server_kubelet_request_duration_seconds`), p99 age of the metrics served by the API
(`metrics_server_api_metric_freshness_seconds`) and p99 duration of a full collection cycle
(`metrics_server_manager_tick_duration_seconds`), all metrics-server's own histograms (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server). The tick must stay well under
the 15 s resolution, otherwise cycles overlap; freshness around the resolution is normal.

panels.title: csr-approver
panels.description: kubelet-csr-approver controller metrics scraped (https://github.com/postfinance/kubelet-csr-approver).

panels.title: Leader
panels.description:
Whether the single replica holds its leader-election lease (`leader_election_master_status`). Only the
leader approves CSRs: 0 = nothing gets approved.

panels.title: Kubelet serving cert
panels.description:
Time left on the kubelet serving certificate (`kubelet_certificate_manager_server_ttl_seconds`):
the outcome this controller exists for. The kubelet requests a new certificate (CSR) at ~70-90 % of the lifetime and this
controller approves it after checking the node name (k8s01) and IP (192.168.68.0/24). Thresholds =
KubeletServerCertificateExpiration (7 d / 1 d).

panels.title: Pending CSRs
panels.description:
CertificateSigningRequests with neither Approved nor Denied condition (kube-state-metrics
`kube_certificatesigningrequest_condition`, https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/tree/main/docs/metrics/cluster/certificatesigningrequest-metrics.md). Normally 0: CSRs exist only
around a rotation and are garbage-collected afterwards. A Pending kubelet-serving CSR that stays = the approver rejected or missed it.

panels.title: Reconciles in range
panels.description:
CSR reconciliations in the selected time range (controller-runtime
`controller_runtime_reconcile_total`, https://book.kubebuilder.io/reference/metrics-reference). Usually 0 for months: work only happens when a CSR is created
(certificate rotation, ~yearly).

panels.title: Reconcile errors in range
panels.description:
Failed reconciliations in the selected range (`controller_runtime_reconcile_errors_total`,
https://book.kubebuilder.io/reference/metrics-reference). > 0 = look at the controller logs: a CSR could not be approved/denied.

panels.title: Server cert renewal errors (24h)
panels.description:
Failed kubelet serving-certificate renewals in 24 h
(`kubelet_server_expiration_renew_errors`, alert KubeletServerCertificateRenewalErrors, https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/kubelet.libsonnet). The
kubelet side of a CSR that was not approved in time.

panels.title: API errors (1h)
panels.description:
Non-2xx answers the controller received from the API server in the last hour
(`rest_client_requests_total`), e.g. 403 if its RBAC to approve CSRs were broken.

panels.title: Provisioner ready
panels.description:
Available replicas of the local-path-provisioner Deployment (kube-state-metrics
`kube_deployment_status_replicas_available`). The project exports no Prometheus metrics (https://github.com/rancher/local-path-provisioner).

panels.title: Restarts (24h)
panels.description: Container restarts of the provisioner in 24 h (kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total).

panels.title: PVCs Pending
panels.description:
PVCs not bound (`kube_persistentvolumeclaim_status_phase{phase="Pending"}`). The local-path
StorageClass uses WaitForFirstConsumer: a PVC is Pending until its first pod is scheduled, so a short Pending during a
deploy is normal; a PVC Pending with its pod already scheduled = provisioning failed (see events below).

panels.title: PVs failed / released
panels.description:
PersistentVolumes in phase Failed or Pending (alert KubePersistentVolumeErrors,
https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/storage_alerts.libsonnet) or Released (claim deleted, directory not cleaned yet; with reclaimPolicy Delete the
helper pod should remove it).

panels.title: PVs local-path
panels.description: PersistentVolumes of StorageClass local-path (kube_persistentvolume_info).

panels.title: Disk free for volumes
panels.description:
Free space on `/`, where /opt/local-path-provisioner lives: the real capacity limit of every
volume (local-path does not enforce PVC sizes). Thresholds as the node-mixin filesystem alerts (see Cluster health).

panels.title: Volume type: local
panels.description:
PVs created as `local` volumes (defaultVolumeType: local; Velero can back them up).
Older PVs created as `hostPath` keep that type until recreated.

panels.title: Volume type: hostPath
panels.description:
PVs created as `hostPath` (before defaultVolumeType: local). Velero file-system backup
skips hostPath volumes, so these are **not backed up** by the node-agent.

panels.title: PVC events
panels.description:
Kubernetes events about PersistentVolumeClaims (Provisioning, ProvisioningSucceeded,
ProvisioningFailed, WaitForFirstConsumer) from Loki (OpenTelemetry k8sobjects receiver, service_name="k8s-events").
ProvisioningFailed tells you why a PVC is stuck.

panels.title: Provisioner logs
panels.description:
Logs of the local-path-provisioner container (Loki). Each volume create/delete is logged,
including the helper pod that creates/removes the directory on the node.

panels.title: Kubernetes scrape targets
panels.description:
Every Prometheus target behind the Kubernetes dashboards, whether it is up and how long the
scrape takes (`up`, `scrape_duration_seconds`, `scrape_samples_scraped`). A target at 0 makes its panels go blank; a scrape
close to the 10 s timeout drops samples.

panels.title: kube-state-metrics list errors
panels.description:
Share of failed LIST calls of kube-state-metrics to the API server over 5 min,
formula of the kube-state-metrics mixin alert KubeStateMetricsListErrors (critical above 1 %,
https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/tree/main/jsonnet/kube-state-metrics-mixin). Needs the telemetry port
scraped (`kube-state-metrics.selfMonitor.enabled`, enabled in this change: **pending scrape** until it is synced).

panels.title: kube-state-metrics watch errors
panels.description:
Same for WATCH calls (`kube_state_metrics_watch_total`, alert
KubeStateMetricsWatchErrors, critical above 1 %). Pending scrape, see the list-errors stat.

panels.title: node-exporter textfile errors
panels.description:
1 when the node-exporter textfile collector failed to read a .prom file
(`node_textfile_scrape_error`, node-mixin alert NodeTextFileCollectorScrapeError, https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin/alerts/alerts.libsonnet).

panels.title: kube-state-metrics & node-exporter resource usage
panels.description:
Working-set memory of kube-state-metrics and node-exporter
(their limits are 192 MiB / 64 MiB in the kps values). kube-state-metrics grows with the number of objects; an OOM kill
blanks most Kubernetes panels.
